metadata.description: Small smoke test dataset for CI validation. Contains 2 synthetic conversations and 10 test questions covering different retrieval scenarios.

turns.text: Hi! I just got back from my trip to Japan. It was absolutely amazing!
turns.speaker: user

turns.text: Welcome back! Japan is wonderful. What cities did you visit?
turns.speaker: assistant

turns.text: I spent 3 days in Tokyo, then took the bullet train to Kyoto for 4 days. The temples in Kyoto were breathtaking, especially Fushimi Inari with all those red torii gates.
turns.speaker: user

turns.text: That sounds like a perfect itinerary! Did you try any memorable food while you were there?
turns.speaker: assistant

turns.text: Oh yes! In Tokyo I had the best ramen of my life at a tiny shop in Shinjuku called Fuunji. Their tsukemen was incredible - rich pork and fish broth. In Kyoto I tried traditional kaiseki cuisine at a restaurant near Gion district.
turns.speaker: user

turns.text: Fuunji is legendary! Kaiseki in Gion sounds like a wonderful cultural experience. What was the highlight of your Kyoto stay?
turns.speaker: assistant

turns.text: Definitely the sunrise at Kiyomizu-dera temple. I woke up at 5am and walked up the hill. The view of the city with the morning mist was magical. Oh, and I also visited the bamboo grove in Arashiyama.
turns.speaker: user

turns.text: Early morning temple visits are the best - fewer crowds and that special light. Did you bring back any souvenirs?
turns.speaker: assistant

turns.text: I've been thinking about switching careers from marketing to software engineering. What do you think?
turns.speaker: user

turns.text: That's a significant transition! What's drawing you to software engineering?
turns.speaker: assistant

turns.text: I've been doing some Python scripting for data analysis at work and I really enjoy it. I like the problem-solving aspect and seeing immediate results. My manager actually encouraged me to explore this path.
turns.speaker: user

turns.text: That's great that you have support from your manager! Python is an excellent starting point. Have you considered what area of software engineering interests you most?
turns.speaker: assistant

turns.text: I'm really interested in backend development and APIs. I've been reading about REST APIs and even built a simple Flask application that connects to a PostgreSQL database. It manages a small inventory system for my friend's bookstore.
turns.speaker: user

turns.text: Building a real application is the best way to learn! Flask with PostgreSQL is a solid stack. What features did you implement?
turns.speaker: assistant

turns.text: It has user authentication with JWT tokens, CRUD operations for books, a search feature, and a simple dashboard showing sales analytics. I deployed it on Heroku using Docker. The whole project took about 3 weeks.
turns.speaker: user

turns.text: Impressive! JWT auth, Docker deployment, and analytics - that covers a lot of backend fundamentals. Have you thought about your learning path forward?
turns.speaker: assistant

turns.text: I'm planning to take the CS50 online course, then maybe a bootcamp. My friend Sarah who works at Google suggested I also learn about data structures and algorithms. She offered to do mock interviews with me next month.
turns.speaker: user

turns.text: CS50 is excellent for building strong foundations. Having a connection at Google for mock interviews is invaluable! What's your timeline for this career switch?
turns.speaker: assistant

questions.answer: User authentication with JWT tokens, CRUD operations for books, a search feature, and a dashboard showing sales analytics.
